source_resources.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition
source_resources.author: Al Sweigart
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Chapter 1; Practice Questions; Appendix B answers
source_resources.version_or_verification_date: Public edition checked 2026-11-01; moving pages may change
source_resources.license: Copyright Al Sweigart; edition-specific reuse terms unverified
source_resources.permission_basis: External hyperlink only; no third-party prose, exercises, code or translations are imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: No prior programming required for Chapter 1; later chapters assume its basic Python concepts.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Beginner teaching and answer-keyed practice before checking exact semantics in the Python reference; selected chapters only, not the book's entire automation stack.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Free HTML; external website may be unavailable. Exact third-edition redistribution terms have not been verified, so no reuse permission is claimed.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Use the original localized explanations, exercises and checks already present in this activity; no external account or purchase is required for that fallback.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Guided Python syntax but assumes programming familiarity; paired with the beginner text rather than used as its replacement.
Lectures and problem sets teach a broader CS1 course; the book offers shorter text-first entry and an answer appendix.

source_resources.author: Python Software Foundation
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Sections  Truth Value Testing, Comparisons, and Mutable Sequence Types
source_resources.permission_basis: Linking only; no source text reproduced.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Normative reference for truthiness, comparison, binding, and mutation behavior.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Online Python documentation may be unavailable offline.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Run the included Python examples and consult the installed interpreter help.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Deeper object-semantics reference than the expression-level drills need; stdtypes keeps the operator-level material in scope.

source_resources.title: Git User Manual: Recording Changes
source_resources.author: Git project
source_resources.permission_basis: Linking only; no source text reproduced.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary reference for inspecting a small diff before a safe commit.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Online book may be unavailable offline.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Use git diff and git status locally; do not commit until the diff is understood.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Command-level flag reference; the Pro Git chapter was selected for its guided walkthrough of inspecting changes before committing.
Friendly commercial walkthrough; the book chapter provides deeper staging/index semantics for the same inspection habit.
